diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Recall $\Delta_{1}(1)=1$ and $\Delta_{\ell}(1)=0$ for $\ell\neq1$
because the Gauss--Hermite rule integrates constant functions exactly.

issues.failure_explanation: The fooling function $p_n(x_1)$ vanishes only where $x_1$ is a root of $H_n$, $n=n_{\overline{\ell}_1}$. The sparse grid also uses nodes whose first coordinates are roots of $H_{n_{\ell_1}}$ for smaller $\ell_1$, and these non-nested roots are generally not zeros of $p_n$. The proof gets $S_\Lambda(h_\Lambda)=0$ only through telescoping with $\Delta_\ell(1)=0$, which uses exactness of the weights on constants. For an arbitrary weighted rule on the same node set, $\sum_i w_i h_\Lambda(\boldsymbol{x}_i)\neq0$ in general. So the lower bound is not shown to be weight-independent.

failure_location.quote: The lower bound is obtained by exploiting the structure of the Gauss--Hermite nodes and is independent of the quadrature weights; consequently, no modification of the weights can improve the rate $N^{-\alpha/2}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to Smolyak constructions whose univariate rules use Gauss–Hermite nodes and integrate constants exactly. Alternatively, construct a new fooling function vanishing at all sparse-grid nodes (the union over levels) and prove the corresponding 1D estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised conclusion that no reweighting of the sparse-grid nodes can beat $N^{-\alpha/2}$ is unsupported. The proven bounds hold only for Gauss–Hermite weights, or for univariate weights exact on constants.
issues.title: Weight-independence of the sparse-grid lower bound is not established
issues.why_classification: The formal theorems survive. However, a headline guarantee in the abstract must either be withdrawn or backed by a new fooling-function argument.

issues.failure_explanation: With $x=\ln n\ge d-1$, the inequality $x^{d-1}\le e^x$ fails for $d\ge4$ near the threshold. For example, $d=4$, $x=3$ gives $27>e^3\approx20.1$. The stated implication is therefore false. The intended conclusion $\ln N\lesssim_d\ln n_{L-d+1}$ still follows from $(\ln n)^{d-1}\le((d-1)/e)^{d-1}n$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use $(\ln n)^{d-1}\le C_d n$ with $C_d=((d-1)/e)^{d-1}$. This gives $N\lesssim_d n^2$ and hence $\ln N\lesssim_d\ln n$, using $\ln n\ge d-1\ge1$.
issues.overall_effect: One step in relating $N$ to $n_{L-d+1}$ is invalid as written. The final lower bound is unaffected once the step is corrected.
issues.title: False inequality $(\ln n)^{d-1}\le n$ for $n\ge e^{d-1}$
issues.why_classification: This is a one-line local fix inside a $\lesssim_d$ estimate. Rate and statement are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
let $\xi_{1},\dots,\xi_{n}$ be the roots of the univariate Hermite
polynomial $H_{n}$ of degree $n$

issues.failure_explanation: $\mathscr{I}_\ell^{\mathrm{uni}}$ interpolates at the zeros of $H_{n_\ell+1}$. Hence $\int\mathscr{I}_{\overline{\ell}_1}^{\mathrm{uni}}(p_n)\rho$ is the $(n+1)$-point Gauss–Hermite rule, not $Q_{\overline{\ell}_1}^{\mathrm{uni}}$, which has $n$ points. Moreover, $p_n$ does not vanish at the zeros of $H_{n+1}$. The identity $\int p_n\rho-Q^{\mathrm{uni}}_{\overline{\ell}_1}(p_n)=\int[p_n-\mathscr{I}(p_n)]\rho$ therefore fails as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either define $\mathscr{I}_\ell^{\mathrm{uni}}$ at the zeros of $H_{n_\ell}$, or use the fooling function $p_{n+1}$ with the $(n+1)$-point Gauss–Hermite rule. Then rerun the same argument; the cost changes by at most a constant.
issues.overall_effect: The reduction of the interpolation lower bound to the quadrature lower bound is invalid with the stated node definition.
issues.title: Interpolation nodes inconsistent with the quadrature and fooling function
issues.why_classification: A consistent choice of nodes restores the argument verbatim, with the same rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The value $b$ controls the truncation error, namely the integral of $f\rho$ over $\mathbb{R}^d\setminus [-\boldsymbol{b},\boldsymbol{b}]$, whereas $Q_N$ controls the numerical integration error.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only establishes decay $|f\rho|\lesssim\rho^{\varepsilon}$ with $\varepsilon<1/2$. This yields truncation error about $e^{-\varepsilon b^2/2}=N^{-\varepsilon\alpha/4}$, not $N^{-\alpha}$. The decay cannot be improved: take $f(\boldsymbol{x})=\psi(x_1-b-1)$, a smooth bump supported outside $[-b,b]$. Then $Q_N(f)=0$, while $I(f)/\|f\|_{H^\alpha_\rho}\gtrsim e^{-(b+1)^2/4-O(b)}=N^{-\alpha/8-o(1)}$. This contradicts the claimed $N^{-\alpha}(\ln N)^{\frac{3\alpha d}{2}+\frac d4}$. The cited [NS22] bound is invoked with a $b$ that does not match the established decay.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose $b=c\sqrt{\alpha\ln N}$ with $c\ge2$ (e.g. $b=2\sqrt{\alpha\ln N}$, as in the digital-net case), matching the decay $\rho^{\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\to1/2$. Then re-verify the [NS22] estimate with this decay parameter to confirm the logarithmic exponent.
issues.overall_effect: The affinely mapped lattice bound, and its entry in the summary theorem, are false as stated. The rate degrades to about $N^{-\alpha/8}$.
issues.title: Truncation parameter $b=\sqrt{(\alpha/2)\ln N}$ too small for rate $N^{-\alpha}$
issues.why_classification: The stated guarantee is false, but a reparametrization of $b$ restores a comparable result with the same polynomial rate. It needs re-verification of the cited estimate, not new architecture.
